Footnotes render ONCE in a single 'Notes & assumptions' section above the contact form; a footnote's source_url may render as a small domain chip, never as a naked URL in body copy. Posture: GREENFIELD Enable-led dual — no authority operates passenger marine transit on this coast; the framing is 'bring the water mode to the corniche economy the Province is already building.' Border Guard route/speed powers render calmly as 'route terms set with the permit.' Road honesty: the EP-1 spine does NOT beat the road off-peak and is never claimed to; EP-2 carries the time-competitive story. fn1.text: The Dareen and Tarout Island development program: a SAR 2.64 billion heritage-coast investment at Qatif — a historic working port, more than 11 heritage sites and protected mangrove habitat — as published by the Saudi Press Agency and the Sharqia Development Authority.

fn2.text: King Fahd Causeway traffic reached a record 33 million passengers in 2024, as communicated by the causeway authority, with a reported single-day record of 136,498 crossings.

fn3.text: Population figures from the 2022 Saudi Census: 5,125,254 residents in the Eastern Province, with about 2.81 million in the merged Dammam–Khobar–Dhahran conurbation.

fn4.text: The Transport General Authority regulates and licenses maritime transport in the Kingdom — vessel registration, navigation permits and operating licenses. The Border Guard is the authority for maritime security and safety: it designates permitted landing and departure sites, lanes, speeds and sailing times, and issues sailing permits. Route terms are set with the permit — no allowance is assumed anywhere on this page.

fn5.text: All map and trip times use a conservative planning basis: slow transit near berths, beaches and shallow bays, service speed only on open coastal legs.

fn6.text: Waterfront program figures as published: the Al Khobar Waterfront second phase adds more than 265,000 square metres along more than four kilometres of frontage, and $3 billion of Eastern Province tourism projects with more than 2,200 hotel rooms were announced in October 2024, as reported via the Saudi Press Agency.

fn7.text: Roadmap items render as reach only: Uqair's heritage port has an announced development program and no passenger landing today, and a Khobar–Bahrain water link appears as roadmap only — no schedule, no economics.

fn8.text: The Dammam–Khobar drive runs about 15 minutes off-peak — on an empty highway the road wins. The spine's case is the corridor's documented peak congestion, the cruise-terminal connection and the corniche-to-corniche experience; the Half Moon Bay line is the time-competitive run when weekend traffic stacks up.

fn9.text: King Abdulaziz Port is the Gulf coast's cruise gateway, developed with Cruise Saudi, with a second terminal and additional berths planned as published.

copy.framing: A first conversation, not a turf conversation. No authority on this coast operates passenger service on the water — the posture is enablement: license a privately financed tier onto the waterfront the Province is already building, under the licensing and permitting regime that already exists.
copy.enable_track: The Transport General Authority licenses the operator and the vessels; the Border Guard sets routes, lanes and sailing terms with the permit; the Municipality grants landings at corniche marinas. Private capital finances the fleet — the ask is licensing and access, not money.
copy.operate_track: Where an authority prefers to procure or concession the service directly, the same corridors specify cleanly — fares, lines and landings defined with the authority against its own waterfront program.

operate_proof_points.proof: One national licensing authority for maritime transport — vessel registration, navigation permits and operator licenses run through a published, digital licensing regime.
Routes, lanes, speeds and sailing times are set with the sailing permit under published maritime security and safety regulations — clear terms, one counterpart on the water.

The corniche landlord and the Province's Vision 2030 development authority are already investing in exactly the waterfronts this network connects — Khobar Waterfront phase two and the SAR 2.64 billion heritage coast.

pillars: Zero-emission electric foiling on a coast whose own development programs protect mangrove habitat and heritage harbors — the compliance-friendly mode by design.

copy.headline: Speed terms here are written into the permit, not a code.
copy.framing: On this coast the regulator sets lanes, speeds and sailing times administratively, corridor by corridor — powers that exist to protect swimmers, moored craft, fishing traffic and shallow heritage bays. A foiling, electric vessel serves those purposes by design.
copy.ask: Our ask: measure us. Where independent wake and noise measurement shows a corridor's purpose is served, set the permit's route and speed terms accordingly — through the process that already exists.

expander.title: What permit terms unlock
body: The Kingdom's maritime security and safety regulations place route, lane, speed and sailing-time decisions with the authority that issues the sailing permit. For a new mode that is an advantage: terms are specified corridor by corridor, with the authority, rather than against a fixed code — and a vessel that makes almost no wake and almost no noise brings measurable evidence to that conversation.

On the heritage bay, low-wake foilborne transit is the mode the development program's own environmental goals call for — the Dareen and Tarout program protects mangrove habitat, and a foilborne hull crosses shallow, sensitive water with minimal wash.

navier_intro.title: Meet the vessel

copy.headline: Zero-emission. Near-silent. Almost no wake.
copy.subline: Navier is a U.S. builder of electric hydrofoil vessels — the traits that matter for harbor rules and harbor neighbors are built into the hull, not bolted on.
copy.body: The N45 Explorer carries 30 passengers at a foilborne cruise speed of about 30 knots, lifted clear of the water for a smooth, wake-free ride. The smaller N30 Quanta carries 8. Foiling cuts energy use by up to ~90% versus a conventional planing hull, and both vessels run near-silent on electric power.

reference.title: Reference

copy.intro: The Eastern Province's water landscape is compact and clearly mandated. We seek conversations — nothing here implies approval, endorsement, or commitment by any body named.

bodies.role: Regulates and develops the Kingdom's maritime transport sector — vessel registration, navigation permits and operating licenses for marine passenger service run through the TGA.

The authority for maritime security and safety: designates permitted landing and departure sites, lanes, speeds and sailing times, and issues sailing permits. Every corridor and timetable is set with the Border Guard.

Manages the Kingdom's ports, including King Abdulaziz Port in Dammam, where Cruise Saudi operates the Gulf coast's cruise gateway — calls at the cruise terminal run under port and berthing agreements.
Landlord of the corniche public realm and its marinas on both waterfronts — the Al Khobar Waterfront program is a municipal development, and corniche landings run through the Municipality.

The Province's Vision 2030 development authority — owner of the Dareen and Tarout Island heritage program and a partner in Khobar tourism development. Its published corridors of interest match this network one to one.

Operator of the 25-km causeway to Bahrain, which carried a record 33 million passengers in 2024. Any future water link to Bahrain respects the causeway's marine zones and appears here as roadmap only.
